title: MATAPA Project - Model of Care with Teamwork, Access, Participation and Coordination
text:
Presentation

MATAPA Project - Model of Care with Teamwork, Access, Participation and Coordination for the Design, implementation and evaluation of a new Primary Health Care model for Mozambique.
This project is already under development in its early stages by the National Institute of Health in partnership with Mozambican and international leaders in Family and Community Medicine.

title: MATAPA Project
text:
Model of Care with Teamwork, Access, Participation and Coordination
Este documento foi criado para organizar as etapas e tarefas proposta para condução nosso projeto para a criação de um Novo Modelo de Cuidado em Moçambique.

title: MATAPA Project
text:
THE PROBLEM
Primary Health Care (PHC) in Mozambique is in urgent need of modernization. Currently, services operate in a fragmented manner: vertical programs — HIV, tuberculosis, malaria, maternal and child health — run in isolation, with no integration between them. A patient with multiple health needs must attend different services, on different days, with different providers. This fragmentation is extremely inefficient: it overwhelms patients and services, leads to missed opportunities for preventive care, and makes continuity of care impossible.

title: MATAPA Project
text:
THE PROPOSAL
The MATAPA Project aims to transform Mozambican PHC from a fragmented, episodic Model of Care into a New Model of Care (NMC) that is comprehensive, longitudinal, and coordinated with other levels of care. This NMC will be organized around multidisciplinary teams responsible for a defined panel of patients, capable of delivering comprehensive services centered on people’s needs.

title: MATAPA Project
text:
METHODOLOGY
The project adopts Participatory Action Research as its methodological approach, structured in five iterative stages: (1) Participatory diagnosis (0–3 months), mapping existing fragmentation and barriers; (2) Co-design of the New Model of Care (3–6 months), translating the diagnosis into feasible and culturally appropriate solutions; (3) Assisted implementation in pilot units (6–18 months), with progressive expansion starting from units with the greatest readiness; (4) Continuous quarterly reflection and adjustment; and (5) Consolidation and institutionalization (18–24 months).
The project will be operationalized through three parallel axes:

Structure & Digital: integrated records via KoBoToolbox, integrated service portfolio, and formative supervision.
Teaching & Capacity Building: on-the-job mentoring, continuing education, and PDSA improvement cycles.
Implementation, Monitoring and Evaluation: quantitative and qualitative indicators, performance dashboards, and monthly quality meetings.

title: MATAPA Project
text:
THEORETICAL FRAMEWORK
The project adopts Participatory Action Research (PAR) as its central methodological approach. PAR is a research methodology in which local stakeholders — health professionals, managers, community leaders, and patients — actively participate in every stage of the process, from problem identification to the evaluation of solutions. This approach is a natural fit for MATAPA because the most sustainable transformations in health services emerge when solutions are co-constructed with those who experience them daily, rather than imposed top-down. The project further integrates internationally recognized frameworks: the 5S-5M-5C framework for analyzing PHC structure, processes, and outcomes; RE-AIM and CFIR for rigorous implementation evaluation; the Quadruple Aim as an outcomes framework (patient experience, team experience, population health, and efficiency); and Barbara Starfield’s essential PHC attributes (access, continuity, comprehensiveness, and coordination).



5S-5M-5C schematic framework

title: MATAPA Project
text:
EXPECTED RESULTS (12–24 MONTHS)
The project aims to achieve the following results across 10 pilot health units in the municipality and province of Maputo: Design and implementation of the New Model of Care: co-construction of an NMC with Mozambican stakeholders, feasible and suited to the local context, including the definition of the service portfolio the NMC can deliver — and a proposal for its expansion — compared to the current Model of Care. Patient enrollment and longitudinal follow-up: registration of patients and families (empanelment), with ongoing follow-up by family physicians and their health teams, identification of the main morbidities in the enrolled population, and longitudinal management of patients and their various health conditions. Monitoring and evaluation: development of individualized monitoring indicators based on each patient’s morbidity profile; identification of the population within key care pathways (maternal and child health, HIV, tuberculosis, malnutrition, malaria, non-communicable diseases); and comparison of care pathway indicators between the enrolled and non-enrolled populations.

title: Models of Care
text:
Concept and Framework
“Model of care” refers to the conceptualization and operationalization of how services are delivered: clinical processes, provider organization, service management, and population management, with clearly defined roles and responsibilities along care pathways. This definition is adopted by WHO/EMRO and is consistent with your initial synthesis distinguishing service selection/organization, delivery platforms, service management, and population management. PHC-oriented models of care

title: Models of Care
text:
PHC-Oriented Models of Care
For PHC-oriented systems, the model is anchored in the Integrated People-Centred Health Services agenda and the PHC Operational Framework (WHO/UNICEF), which detail functions, levers, and measurement for translating vision into operation. Take home messages from the implementation of the primary health care measurement and improvement (PHCMI) initiative in the WHO Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR)

title: Models of Care
section: Organization and Types of Models of Care
text:
Organization and Types of Models of Care
Although the components of a MoC may vary, they generally encompass: the selection and organization of services (including the essential service package); the definition of roles and functions of service delivery platforms; service management (including supportive supervision and multidisciplinary teams); and population health management (including the empanelment system — also called alistamento or carterização in Brazilian Portuguese — and community engagement).

title: Models of Care
text:
Integration with the 5S-5M-5C Framework
The 5S-5M-5C, proposed by Bitton et al. based on the PHCPI framework, is an operational shortcut: 5 inputs (Systems, Space, Staff, Stuff, Surveillance) activated by 5 mechanisms ( Multidisciplinary teams, Motivation, Measurement, Monitoring, Management) to produce 5 quality functions (First Contact, Continuity, Comprehensiveness, Coordination, Person-Centred Care). The framework helps move beyond investing solely in inputs and toward prioritizing delivery mechanisms—exactly the emphasis of your text. The 5S-5M-5C schematic: transforming primary care inputs to outcomes in low-income and middle-income countries
How to use in practice: when redesigning a MoC, derive a “blueprint” where each proposed intervention makes explicit which M among the 5M activates which C among the 5C and which S need to be in place (e.g., multidisciplinary team + supportive supervision → coordination and continuity; requires a unified health record and integrated scheduling).

title: Models of Care
section: Why “How” We Organize Care Changes Outcomes
text:
Why “How” We Organize Care Changes Outcomes

Brazil (national longitudinal analysis): municipalities with higher-quality PHC — more qualified professionals and CHWs integrated into teams — achieved additional reductions in hospitalizations and mortality (diabetes, CVD, leprosy), beyond the effect of expanding access. In other words, the model design matters, not just coverage. The quality of alternative models of primary health care and morbidity and mortality in Brazil: a national longitudinal analysis
PHC–mental health/behavioral conditions integration: collaborative team models (family physician + case manager + specialist) improve clinical outcomes and reduce emergency/hospital utilization; in children/adolescents, meta-analyses show an advantage of collaborative care over usual care. Implementing High-Quality Primary Care: Rebuilding the Foundation of Health Care - Integrated Primary Care Delivery
Nurse-led models and work organization: reviews report reduced medication errors and improved pain outcomes in “team nursing,” with mixed effects on other outcomes—reinforcing the importance of implementation fidelity and context. Models of care in nursing: a systematic review
Equity and persons with disabilities in Brazil: a multicenter study (REDECIN-BRASIL) shows that the FHS model is associated with a higher frequency of practices targeting persons with disabilities compared to the traditional PHC model. Primary health organization models and care practices for people with disabilities in Brazil

title: Models of Care
text:
Types/Architectures That Recurrently Appear

Community-anchored PHC (FHS, FPA/EMRO), with empanelment, home visits, coordination with specialized care and social services. PHC-oriented models of care
Hub-and-spoke in primary care networks (e.g., experiences documented by R4D and partners), to consolidate clinical and logistical capacity in “hubs” with matrix support to the “spokes.” 5 principles for building an innovative primary health care model
Horizontal/vertical integration (e.g., rare condition care coordination; child-to-adult transitions), with explicit roles for navigation, case management, and referral/counter-referral agreements. Development of models of care coordination for rare conditions: a qualitative study
Post-2030 hybrid models (home-centered, low-friction digital, multidisciplinary teams with community outreach), identified as a strategic direction for multimorbidity. Models of global primary care post-2030 - PMC

title: Models of Care
text:
Design and Evaluation Tools

Circle of Care Modeling structures stakeholder discussions starting from the patient, useful for avoiding preconceived supply-side solutions. Circle of care modelling: an approach to assist in reasoning about healthcare change using a patient-centric system
MoC Evaluation Tool (MCET) offers a 5-component checklist for comparing/adapting models under adoption. Evaluating models of healthcare delivery using the Model of Care Evaluation Tool (MCET)
Care process frameworks (rapid task analysis) support the design of “real work” in clinics and territories. A novel and practical care process framework to inform model of care development
WHO/EMRO standards and implementation materials (regional initiative) provide steps, deliverables, and examples for PHC-oriented models of care. Designing and implementing primary health care-oriented models of care in the Eastern Mediterranean Region: Regional initiative for transforming vision into action

title: Models of Care
section: Applied Examples by Care Pathway (What Changes on the Ground)
text:
Applied Examples by Care Pathway (What Changes on the Ground)

Chronic conditions/multimorbidity: integrated models with panel management, extended consultations, intensification of protocols, clinical pharmacists, and telemonitoring show gains in process/utilization and, in mature settings, in outcomes. Systematic review of integrated models of health care delivered at the primary-secondary interface: how effective is it and what determines effectiveness?
Oncology and survivorship: survivorship care programs (SCPs) and structured navigation are feasible but require time and resources; when well implemented, they improve coordination and patient experience. Models of Care in Providing Comprehensive Healthcare on Cancer Survivors: A Scoping Review with a TIDieR Checklist Analysis
Elderly and home-based care: reviews of home/community-based arrangements (case management, integrated care, consumer-directed) describe effects on service utilization and autonomy, depending on local arrangements and social integration. A systematic review of different models of home and community care services for older persons

title: Models of Care
section: Practical Roadmap (in 6 Steps) for (Re)designing a PHC-Oriented MoC
text:
Practical Roadmap (in 6 Steps) for (Re)designing a PHC-Oriented MoC

Define population, scope, and goals (Triple/Quadruple Aim + equity). List tracer conditions and pathway indicators (time to diagnosis, loss to follow-up, readmissions). Build on the WHO/EMRO definition to avoid confusing “programs” with “models.” PHC-oriented models of care
Map the journey and backstage (journey + service blueprint), making roles, ICT, regulation rules, and hand-offs explicit. Mark where each 5M will be activated. Circle of care modelling: an approach to assist in reasoning about healthcare change using a patient-centric system
Design the team and clinical governance (multidisciplinary teams, expanded nursing scope, clinical pharmacy, mental health), with supportive supervision and protocols. Models of care in nursing: a systematic review
Population management and empanelment, with active case-finding, risk stratification, navigation, and integration with social services; ensure measurement and monitoring that are useful for decision-making (the two central “Ms” of the 5M). The 5S-5M-5C schematic: transforming primary care inputs to outcomes in low-income and middle-income countries
Implement in short cycles (PDSA) and evaluate with standardized tools (MCET; WHO/UNICEF indicators for PHC). Evaluating models of healthcare delivery using the Model of Care Evaluation Tool (MCET)
Plan for scale and adaptation using MoC design principles (fit with the existing system; network collaboration; focus on clear needs; continuous learning; investment in people). 5 principles for building an innovative primary health care model

title: Models of Care
section: Common Risks and How to Mitigate Them
text:
Common Risks and How to Mitigate Them

Subjective construction and “paper model” → use data and validation with users/teams; connect each intervention to an M and a C from the 5S-5M-5C; track with pathway and experience indicators. The 5S-5M-5C schematic: transforming primary care inputs to outcomes in low-income and middle-income countries
Low attention to equity/PROGRESS-Plus → incorporate determinants (residence, race/ethnicity, occupation, gender, education, income, social capital, disability) into panel design and care flows. Take home messages from the implementation of the primary health care measurement and improvement (PHCMI) initiative in the WHO Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR)
Implementation fidelity → invest in supervision, clinical IT, and clear roles; the evidence of positive effects depends on “how” the model is operated. Models of care in nursing: a systematic review


Examples and Organizational Approaches:

Family Practice Approach (FPA): This approach is being implemented in several countries of the Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR). It transforms the service delivery approach from individual to family-based and integrated. The FPA seeks to strengthen the link between community health and facility-based services.
Hub-and-Spoke Model (Ghana): In Ghana, the Preferred Primary Provider (PPP) Networks initiative uses the Hub-and-Spoke model. In this model, four to five smaller zones (Spokes) connect to a larger and better-equipped Health Center or CHPS (Community Health Planning and Services) facility (Hub), forming a group practice to provide comprehensive care to a defined population. This model emphasizes collaboration among providers rather than competition.
PHC Organizational Models in Brazil: A study compared the Traditional PHC Model with the Family Health Strategy (FHS) model. The FHS model showed a positive and statistically significant association with a higher frequency of practices targeting Persons with Disabilities (PwD), such as prenatal follow-up, home-based care, and health education, compared to the Traditional PHC Model.

title: Models of Care
text:
Theoretical Frameworks: The 5S-5M-5C Schematic
The 5S-5M-5C schematic is a simplified conceptual model, derived from the Primary Health Care Performance Initiative (PHCPI), that details the essential service delivery mechanisms needed to transform inputs into functional and equitable PHC systems. The main objective is to transform system inputs into desired PHC outcomes.
The 5S-5M-5C schematic proposes that the presence of 5S inputs and their effective utilization through 5M mechanisms will produce the 5C functions, ensuring effective coverage of high-quality PHC services and yielding better population health.

1. The 5S (Inputs)
The 5S represent the fundamental health system components that must be available and equipped. They expand the 4S (Systems, Space, Staff, Stuff) proposed by Paul Farmer, adding Surveillance:

S ystems: Refers to the governance and information systems required for care delivery.
S pace: Includes the physical infrastructure of PHC facilities.
S taff (Workforce): Involves available, appropriately trained, and funded providers.
S tuff: Refers to the necessary medicines, supplies, and equipment.
S urveillance: The capacity to identify emerging threats and continuously assess/respond to community needs over time.



2. The 5M (Service Delivery Mechanisms)
The 5M are the crucial service mechanisms that bridge the gap between Inputs (5S) and Functions (5C), ensuring that PHC is effective and equitable:

M ulti-disciplinary teams: Involve the formation, training, and support of provider teams (including physicians, nurses, community health workers, and other disciplines) working together to meet individual and population needs.
M otivation: Extrinsic levers (such as adequate salaries and performance-based incentives) and intrinsic ones (such as supportive supervision) are needed to sustain competent and effective care delivery.
M easurement: Continuous data collection to inform and drive improvement. It is necessary to reduce the large number of disease-specific indicators and leverage advances in information systems.
M onitoring: Active and regular use of measurement data to drive continuous quality improvement.
M anagement: Population health and facility management systems must coordinate efficient care. Population health management is imperative for the proactive assessment and improvement of the health of entire populations, linking services between communities and facilities.



3. The 5C (Quality Functions)
The 5C represent the functions that a successful PHC system must deliver. They expand Barbara Starfield’s 4C (First-Contact Accessibility, Continuity, Comprehensiveness, and Coordination) with the addition of Person-Centred Care:

C ontact (Accessibility): Ensuring that services are accessible when and where people need them and in a financially affordable manner.
C ontinuity: Fostering ongoing, longitudinal relationships between patient and provider.
C omprehensiveness: Optimizing the provision of preventive, chronic management, and acute curative services to meet health needs.
C oordination: Optimizing the individual’s journey through a complex health system.
C o-centered (Person-centred): Means that patient needs and preferences are respected, building trust in the PHC system.

For PHC development, it is crucial to prioritize investments and research in the 5M mechanisms, as the historical focus solely on inputs (4S’s) through vertical programs has been insufficient to achieve UHC in a sustainable and equitable manner.



5S5M5C schematic model


It is important to remember that the 5S-5M-5C framework is not a ready-made answer for how to organize a Model of Care, but rather a framework with explicit domains so that, when planning a health service, no important aspect is left out.
The 5S-5M-5C framework is fully consistent with WHO operational definitions and with the available evidence: PHC-oriented models of care work when they activate delivery mechanisms (teams, supervision, measurement/monitoring, population management) on an adequate input base—and when they are designed and evaluated with explicit tools (journey/blueprint, MCET, WHO/UNICEF indicators). Use the 5S-5M-5C as an accountability matrix: each proposed change must declare which M activates which C and which S sustain it—and then measure what it promised.

title: Como usar personas e itinerários terapêuticos para melhorar o sistema de saúde
text:
Por que usar personas em trajetórias de cuidado
Em saúde, personas (perfis hipotéticos porém realistas) ajudam equipes a visualizar usuários, contextualizar suas experiências e gerar soluções alinhadas a atitudes, emoções, motivações e metas ao longo do itinerário terapêutico. Revisões recentes mostram crescimento acelerado do uso de personas desde 2019, sobretudo em países de alta renda, com aplicações em eHealth, redesenho de serviços e entendimento de comportamentos de uso. The use of personas to involve consumers in healthcare co-design: a scoping review
Além de fomentar empatia e manter “o paciente no centro” nas discussões, personas funcionam como instrumento participativo quando o recrutamento direto é difícil (ex.: doença grave, tempo limitado). Elas também protegem a confidencialidade, pois permitem discutir necessidades sem expor dados pessoais.The use of personas to involve consumers in healthcare co-design: a scoping review

title: Como usar personas e itinerários terapêuticos para melhorar o sistema de saúde
section: Evidências e casos de uso relevantes
text:
Evidências e casos de uso relevantes

eHealth dor crônica — revisão sistemática descreve como personas orientam decisões de design (conteúdo, formato, engajamento) em intervenções digitais para dor crônica, apoiando aderência e personalização. Using Personas in the development of eHealth interventions for chronic pain: A scoping review and narrative synthesis
Oncologia pediátrica — no desenvolvimento de um serviço digital de apoio entre pares para sobreviventes de câncer infantil, personas de crianças (cocriadas com pacientes) guiaram escolhas de design e aumentaram a empatia da equipe. Effects of Using Child Personas in the Development of a Digital Peer Support Service for Childhood Cancer Survivors
Atenção Primária à Saúde (Health TAPESTRY) — método “persona-cenário” para co-desenhar intervenção complexa com idosos, provedores e voluntários; útil para mapear necessidades, fluxos e pontos de fricção na jornada (acesso, continuidade, coordenação). Health TAPESTRY: co-designing interprofessional primary care programs for older adults using the persona-scenario method
Equidade no acesso digital — personas que capturam desvantagens interseccionais (idade, baixa renda, alfabetização digital, multicomorbidades) ajudam a adaptar a APS remota/digital a perfis vulneráveis. Developing user personas to capture intersecting dimensions of disadvantage in older patients who are marginalised: a qualitative study
Co-design e trabalho em equipes integradas — personas e artefatos de co-design apoiam entendimento compartilhado das necessidades de informação e pontos de transição entre serviços (ex.: ICS/integração). Co-design with Integrated Care Teams: Establishing Information Needs
EBD (Experience-Based Design) — guias NHS e estudos do IHI mostram como narrativas/“touchpoints de emoção” e, quando usados, personas e journey maps estruturam melhorias em experiência e segurança. NHS - Experience based design Using patient and staff experience to design better healthcare services

title: Como usar personas e itinerários terapêuticos para melhorar o sistema de saúde
section: Como personas se conectam ao itinerário terapêutico
text:
Como personas se conectam ao itinerário terapêutico
Personas tornam visíveis as etapas críticas (pré-busca de cuidado → acesso → diagnóstico → tratamento → transições → seguimento), os atores (paciente, cuidador, APS, especializada, regulação), os recursos (transporte, conectividade, fármacos) e os modos de contato (presencial, telessaúde). Em redesign de linhas de cuidado (por exemplo, metas como o “Faster Diagnosis Standard” de 28 dias), personas ajudam a testar cenários “e se…?” e identificar gargalos (marcação, preparação de exames, devolutiva de resultados). Case Study – Introducing the Role of Pathway Navigator to the South East Region Cancer Alliances – a current project

title: Como usar personas e itinerários terapêuticos para melhorar o sistema de saúde
section: Exemplos práticos de aplicação (com caminhos para implementação)
text:
Exemplos práticos de aplicação (com caminhos para implementação)

APS e acesso digital (Brasil/APS remota)


Personas: “Dona Maria, 72, baixa escolaridade, múltiplas DCNT, smartphone compartilhado;” “Seu José, 58, trabalhador informal, dados móveis intermitentes”.
Uso: mapear barreiras de triagem digital, agendamento e renovação de receitas; co-desenhar fluxos multimodais (telefone + WhatsApp + presencial), mensagens em linguagem simples, e apoio de navegação comunitária.
Evidência: personas para vulnerabilidade digital em APS e persona-cenário em intervenção com idosos. Husain L et al. BJGP, 2024. Developing user personas to capture intersecting disadvantage in remote/digital primary care


Oncologia (linha de diagnóstico e tratamento)


’Personas: “mulher 45a com cuidado infantil, renda instável, sintomas intermitentes”; “homem 67a rural, sem carro, baixa literacia em saúde”.
Uso: journey maps por persona → tempos de espera por etapa; prototipar papel de “navegador de percurso”, pré-consulta remota para preparo de exames e sinalização ativa de faltas.
Contexto e guias: padrões de via rápida (28/62 dias), casos NHS de redesenho de vias; personas aumentam a aderência da equipe a soluções centradas no paciente.Case Study – Introducing the Role of Pathway Navigator to the South East Region Cancer Alliances – a current project


Condições crônicas e autocuidado digital


Personas orientam conteúdo, feedback e escalonamento clínico em apps de dor crônica/condições crônicas, aumentando relevância e engajamento ao longo da trajetória (auto-monitoramento → APS → especializada). Using Personas in the development of eHealth interventions: chronic pain.

title: Como usar personas e itinerários terapêuticos para melhorar o sistema de saúde
section: Passo a passo recomendado (rápido e acionável)
text:
Passo a passo recomendado (rápido e acionável)

Defina escopo da linha de cuidado (ex.: “suspeita-diagnóstico-início de tratamento em câncer de cabeça e pescoço”). Liste metas (p.ex., tempo até diagnóstico, taxa de não comparecimento, continuidade). Using Lean to redesign pathways
Colete dados mistos: entrevistas/observação, bases administrativas, tempos de fluxo, queixas, reclamações, dados de desigualdade. (EBD/EBCD). NHS - Experience based design Using patient and staff experience to design better healthcare services
Crie personas ancoradas em evidências (não estereótipos): sintetize padrões de necessidades e comportamentos; valide com usuários e equipe clínica.Health TAPESTRY: co-designing interprofessional primary care programs for older adults using the persona-scenario method
Incorpore equidade com PROGRESS-Plus na criação das personas (residência, raça/etnia, ocupação, gênero, escolaridade, renda, capital social, deficiência etc.).Cochrane Equity. PROGRESS-Plus | Cochrane Equity
Mapeie a jornada por persona: passos, emoções, dores, pontos de handoff, canais, prazos; identifique gargalos e riscos de segurança. (Use oficinas de co-design). Co-design with Integrated Care Teams: Establishing Information Needs
Coconstrua soluções: navegação de percurso, checklists de preparo, mensagens segmentadas, triagem combinada digital/presencial, “one-stop clinics”, ajustes de agenda/regulação. (Teste com cenários de cada persona). Re-designing Cancer Pathways - Fab NHS Stuff
Implemente e meça: defina indicadores por persona (tempo até diagnóstico, completude de exames, readmissões, experiência relatada) e retroalimente o desenho. (EBD/EBCD). NHS - Experience based design Using patient and staff experience to design better healthcare services

title: Como usar personas e itinerários terapêuticos para melhorar o sistema de saúde
text:
Limitações e como mitigá-las

Construção subjetiva/sesgos → mitigar com dados reais, métodos transparentes, validação com usuários, e atualização periódica. The use of personas to involve consumers in healthcare co-design: a scoping review
Custo/tempo → usar templates e kits (NHS Horizons/EBD), amostras teóricas enxutas e priorização por alto impacto no fluxo. Personas: Using psychographic analysis to better understand groups of users. What are personas?
Baixa representação de determinantes (raça/etnia, escolaridade, renda, religião) → exigir checklist PROGRESS-Plus em cada persona e metas de inclusão. The use of personas to involve consumers in healthcare co-design: a scoping review

Valaitis R et al. Can Fam Physician. 2014 Mar;60(3):294-296.(Persona-scenario exercise for co-designing primary care interventions
Husain L et al. BJGP, 2024. Developing user personas to capture intersecting disadvantage in remote/digital primary care
NHS Institute. Experience-Based Design: Guide & Toolkit. NHS - Experience based design Using patient and staff experience to design better healthcare services
IHI/Commonwealth Fund. Experience-Based Co-Design of Health Care Services — Case Study. Experience-Based Co-Design of Health Care Services
Personas — how are they used in healthcare improvement? Este documento do NHS Horizons explica o que são personas e como usá-las no desenho de melhorias do sistema de saúde. A persona is a fictional character created to represent a group of users, typically patients or staff groups. Personas: Using psychographic analysis to better understand groups of users. What are personas?
Cochrane Equity. PROGRESS-Plus | Cochrane Equity

Em síntese
Personas são especialmente úteis quando combinadas com mapeamento de jornada e co-design para redesenhar itinerários terapêuticos: tornam visíveis barreiras e determinantes, orientam soluções específicas por perfil e facilitam decisões que reduzem tempos, melhoram continuidade e ampliam equidade. O ganho vem menos do “artefato em si” e mais do processo disciplinado de criar, validar, usar e medir personas ao longo de toda a linha de cuidado. The use of personas to involve consumers in healthcare co-design: a scoping review

title: Como usar personas e itinerários terapêuticos para melhorar o sistema de saúde
section: The use of personas to involve consumers in healthcare co-design: a scoping review
text:
The use of personas to involve consumers in healthcare co-design: a scoping review
Forças das personas
As personas foram relatadas como uma ferramenta eficaz para promover uma abordagem centrada no usuário no co-design e também como um valioso instrumento participativo. Elas foram usadas para manter o grupo de usuários — geralmente pacientes — em foco durante as discussões sobre ideias e soluções.
Por exemplo, foi relatado que as ideias de protótipos para um serviço digital de apoio entre pares foram projetadas para se alinhar com os objetivos, preferências e atitudes das personas e superar as frustrações descritas nelas. As personas também foram apontadas como geradoras de empatia e como formas de privilegiar experiências enquanto histórias a serem compartilhadas.
As equipes de projeto usaram personas como um substituto das perspectivas dos pacientes quando o recrutamento de participantes era desafiador ou quando o estado de saúde do grupo dificultava sua participação, garantindo que suas necessidades fossem consideradas no co-design.
Como instrumento participativo, as personas foram descritas como uma ferramenta que ajudava os participantes a criar e inovar, a evocar ideias ricas, a facilitar o envolvimento dos participantes, a pensar além de suas próprias experiências e a gerar um senso de pertencimento quando participavam da criação das personas.
Em vários estudos, foi mantido um nível de confidencialidade quando os participantes descreviam as experiências, necessidades e ideias das personas sem precisar revelar suas próprias informações pessoais ou experiências.
As equipes de pesquisa ou de projeto usaram as personas como uma ferramenta para especificar os resultados ou aspectos que queriam explorar, para capturar múltiplas experiências de usuários, como instrumento de consenso e como auxílio à comunicação.
Limitações das personas
As limitações das personas foram relatadas em alguns estudos. Parte deles observou que a construção subjetiva das personas pode resultar em representações tendenciosas ou menos autênticas; outros descreveram o desenvolvimento das personas como algo que consome muitos recursos e tempo; e um estudo reconheceu que o uso de personas e cenários limitou a participação a pessoas que sabiam ler em inglês.
Em todos os estudos, os consumidores estiveram envolvidos nos processos de identificar, analisar, definir e projetar. De particular interesse para esta revisão, as personas foram usadas para facilitar o envolvimento dos consumidores em todos os processos de co-design: identificar, analisar, definir e projetar.
Na maioria dos casos, as personas foram usadas em múltiplos processos de co-design. O uso de personas tanto nos processos de análise quanto de definição foi a combinação mais frequente. Um estudo relatou o uso de personas em todos os quatro processos de co-design.
Os resultados mostraram que os determinantes adicionais do modelo PROGRESS-Plus — como a orientação sexual — foram relatados em mais de 90% dos estudos. Os fatores menos relatados foram religião, raça ou etnia, posição socioeconômica e escolaridade.
Características das personas
O uso relatado de personas para envolver consumidores no co-design em saúde aumentou acentuadamente desde 2019. Os estudos revisados foram, em geral, realizados em países de alta renda e descreveram o desenvolvimento de soluções tecnológicas ou pesquisas para compreender atitudes e comportamentos. Personas são usuários ou clientes hipotéticos, porém realistas. Observamos que sua autenticidade derivava de dados de pesquisa ou da contribuição de pessoas usuárias. Contudo, houve grande variação em como as personas foram projetadas, apresentadas e utilizadas como ferramenta de co-design.
As personas foram empregadas com sucesso para elevar a centralidade do consumidor no co-design por meio da empatia provocada por uma compreensão profunda de atitudes, emoções, motivações e metas. Serviram para visualizar usuários, contextualizar suas experiências e gerar soluções que atendessem às suas necessidades. Por exemplo, Ha e colaboradores criaram usuários virtuais de uma plataforma de serviços de saúde digital para identificar requisitos e prever comportamentos quando o novo serviço fosse implementado.
Valaitis e colaboradores distinguiram personas de outros métodos, como grupos focais e entrevistas, que tradicionalmente envolvem consumidores como “consultores” que respondem a perguntas e agendas de pesquisadores. Com personas, as necessidades, ideias e soluções passaram a ser centradas nos consumidores e contrariaram visões ingênuas, estereotipadas ou desatualizadas por vezes presentes em equipes de design ou outros atores do co-design.
Price e colaboradores relataram uma abordagem de “modelagem do círculo de cuidado” para considerar mudanças no sistema de saúde. Os autores descreveram como as personas forneceram uma estrutura de discussão centrada no paciente: as partes interessadas examinavam benefícios, desafios e riscos de diferentes opções de cuidado referindo-se às personas durante as discussões. As personas ajudaram a focar nas necessidades dos pacientes e nas lacunas de serviço, em vez de requisitos organizacionais e soluções preconcebidas.
O estudo de Wärnestål e colaboradores oferece um exemplo da atenção e compreensão despertadas na equipe por personas autênticas e relacionáveis. A equipe sueca usou personas para desenvolver um serviço digital de apoio entre pares para sobreviventes de câncer infantil. As personas de crianças foram criadas com a participação delas e funcionaram como uma ferramenta eficaz para decisões ao longo do processo de design. A equipe relatou que as personas evocaram soluções mais empáticas do que se estivessem projetando para “usuários” de modo abstrato.
As personas também foram um instrumento participativo valioso para estimular discussão e apoiar participantes do co-design a expressarem opiniões. Inspiraram criatividade e impulsionaram a inovação em sessões de co-design por meio de debates vibrantes. Quando usadas em sessões com consumidores junto a outros atores como parceiros iguais, permitiram considerar múltiplas perspectivas; os participantes podiam recorrer às próprias experiências e, ao mesmo tempo, “calçar os sapatos de outra pessoa” e pensar além de si. As personas ofereceram privacidade: os participantes podiam projetar nelas suas necessidades e ideias sem revelar informações pessoais ou vivências — algo especialmente importante em temas sensíveis como comportamento sexual e saúde mental e em populações prioritárias como famílias em situação de adversidade e pessoas que usam drogas injetáveis. As personas também foram úteis como meio de comunicação dentro das equipes e para divulgação externa dos projetos.
Embora os estudos tenham sido majoritariamente positivos, foram descritas limitações quanto ao escopo das personas e potencial de vieses. Também se observou que desenvolvê-las e aplicá-las no co-design requer tempo e recursos.
O uso de personas nos processos de co-design
Utilizamos o referencial apresentado por Vargas e colaboradores para registrar os processos de co-design com envolvimento de consumidores e acompanhar sua amplitude (Figura 3), embora não tenhamos avaliado a profundidade do envolvimento nem definido um limiar mínimo para relatá-lo (Tabela 3). Observamos que o processo de identificar foi pouco descrito. Identificar atores relevantes e o contexto em que um projeto opera cria oportunidades para explorar a diversidade de valores e experiências que podem influenciar necessidades e soluções em saúde. Processos subsequentes de co-design podem ficar limitados sem uma consideração generosa da complexidade contextual.
Também se verificou envolvimento relativamente limitado dos consumidores no processo de design, o que pode levar à implementação de soluções que não centralizem o consumidor e se mostrem insustentáveis. As personas foram amplamente relatadas nos processos de analisar e definir (Figura 3). Usá-las para compreender experiências de consumidores e demais atores, priorizar problemas e gerar soluções criativas e novas se alinha aos atributos das personas como ferramenta participativa eficaz que aprimora a experiência do usuário.
Hall e colaboradores descreveram com elegância o co-design de um hub integrado de saúde e assistência social para famílias em situação de adversidade. Consumidores e provedores participaram do desenvolvimento de personas e de oficinas de co-design para desenhar o modelo do hub, de modo que o envolvimento do consumidor ficou evidente em todos os processos de co-design de Vargas. O envolvimento construiu confiança comunitária e senso de pertencimento ao modelo. As personas foram empregadas em todos os processos de co-design, exceto no de identificar, e funcionaram como ferramenta de storytelling eficaz para construir empatia e adotar uma abordagem centrada no usuário ao longo de todo o projeto. A satisfação com a cultura participativa das oficinas, medida por um instrumento de avaliação de engajamento de pacientes e público, foi muito alta, e os participantes apreciaram o caráter prático do co-design.
Envolvimento de populações prioritárias
Usamos a ferramenta PROGRESS-Plus para verificar se as personas contemplavam ou envolviam consumidores que enfrentam fatores conhecidos por limitar sua participação plena nos serviços de saúde e em seu desenho. Constatamos que fatores como ocupação, capital social, gênero, local de residência e determinantes adicionais, como deficiência, foram relatados em pelo menos metade dos estudos. Por outro lado, religião, raça/etnia, posição socioeconômica e escolaridade — todos determinantes importantes da saúde — foram pouco relatados. As razões não são claras, mas é possível que personas sejam apresentadas com características pouco definidas para torná-las relacionáveis a um público amplo e que o recrutamento de consumidores de populações prioritárias para sessões de co-design seja desafiador.
Esse achado sinaliza a necessidade de incluir deliberadamente comunidades diversas e subatendidas no co-design e reforça a importância de seu envolvimento na etapa de identificar. Priorizar a participação de grupos prioritários em todos os processos de co-design e usar ferramentas criativas, como personas, para apoiar essa participação pode resultar em intervenções aceitáveis, adequadas ao contexto e potencialmente mais eficazes. Maenhout e colaboradores encontraram viabilidade de cocriação com adolescentes com deficiência intelectual quando se usam métodos criativos. De modo semelhante, em um estudo com pessoas com doença de Parkinson, demência ou afasia, Neate e colaboradores observaram que personas cocriadas incentivaram pessoas com necessidades diversas a se engajar no co-design. O envolvimento de consumidores no processo de identificar e uma abordagem de co-design baseada em fortalezas — que enfatiza recursos e capacidades dos consumidores — podem favorecer inovações em saúde que atendam melhor às populações prioritárias.

title: Therapeutic Itinerary
text:
What It Is and Why Use It
Patient Journey Mapping (PJM) is a set of methods for visualizing and describing how people enter, move through, and exit services, combining visual maps, narratives, and tables that portray experiences, transitions, and interactions along the care pathway. Recent reviews highlight the growth of PJM since 2015, the variety of approaches, and its usefulness for identifying gaps and guiding new user-centered models of care—although methodological reporting remains inconsistent. Patient journey mapping: emerging methods for understanding and improving patient experiences of health systems and services - PubMed
PJM directly connects with people-centered care and network integration agendas by making explicit the needs, emotions, goals, and barriers at each stage of the journey. This makes it a bridge between patient experience, process improvement, and health policy. Integrated people-centred care - GLOBAL

title: Therapeutic Itinerary
section: Most Commonly Used Methods and Artifacts
text:
Most Commonly Used Methods and Artifacts
Journey maps: timeline with stages, touchpoints, emotions/pain points, expectations, and associated evidence. Reporting and conducting patient journey mapping research in healthcare: A scoping review - PubMed

Service blueprinting: adds “backstage” elements (processes, roles, ICT, rules), facilitating operational prioritization and the design of digital/omnichannel flows. Using Journey Mapping and Service Blueprinting to Design Digital Health Behavior Change Innovations: A Scoping Review
Emotional/experience mapping: maps emotional highs and lows to guide experience and safety interventions. Lifestyle Medicine Accelerator – Co-design Toolkit
Process mapping/lean: captures the “as is” with multidisciplinary teams; useful for finding waste, bottlenecks, and handoff risks. Conventional process mapping - aqua.nhs.uk
PJM + data: integration with process mining (EHR) and simulation to quantify flows/times and test “what if…?” scenarios. A Data-Driven Approach to Support the Understanding and Improvement of Patients’ Journeys: A Case Study Using Electronic Health Records of an Emergency Department
Co-design/EBCD: uses narratives (patients/professionals) to co-create solutions; guides and evidence of impact are available. Experience-Based Co-Design of Health Care Services

The most recent methodological synthesis proposes six steps for conducting PJM, illustrated with cardiovascular cases: define objective/scope; collect data; build the map; identify opportunities; co-create solutions; and plan evaluation/implementation. Patient journey mapping: emerging methods for understanding and improving patient experiences of health systems and services - PubMed

title: Therapeutic Itinerary
section: Evidence and Applied Cases (Service Improvement and Model of Care)
text:
Evidence and Applied Cases (Service Improvement and Model of Care)

Emergency department access and experience: journey maps were used to improve communication with patients/families in the ED and guide flow changes; reviews on ED flow show that reducing times is associated with better outcomes, and simulation studies show significant decreases in triage times when design is adjusted based on the map. The patient journey map: Improving the emergency department communication experience for patients and their family and friends
Oncology journey: mappings have identified gaps in screening-diagnosis-treatment stages, pointing to navigation solutions, pre-consultation preparation, and results communication; a specific review on breast cancer systematizes PJM uses for improving care pathways. Breast cancer patient experiences through a journey map
Chronic and digital care: blueprinting + journey mapping have been applied to digital interventions for behavior change and self-care, structuring support points, channels (app/phone/in-person), and team integrations. Using Journey Mapping and Service Blueprinting to Design Digital Health Behavior Change Innovations: A Scoping Review
Human-centered design and QI: studies and guides show PJM as a trigger for improvement focus (prioritization) and patient-centered design; a classic patient-centered mapping case (mixed methods) directed QI efforts toward experience. Creation of a Patient-Centered Journey Map to Improve the Patient Experience: A Mixed Methods Approach
Surveillance and viral hepatitis (Asia): qualitative PJM methodology in Vietnam and the Philippines informed the co-design of people-centered interventions adapted to local context. Putting people at the center: methods for patient journey mapping of viral hepatitis services across two LMICs in the Asia Pacific

title: Therapeutic Itinerary
section: How to Apply (Practical Roadmap for Redesigning the Itinerary)
text:
How to Apply (Practical Roadmap for Redesigning the Itinerary)

Define the problem, scope, and goals Choose the care pathway (e.g., “suspicion → diagnosis → treatment initiation”) and indicators (time to diagnosis, absenteeism, continuity). Use a logic model and “Triple/Quadruple Aim” objectives. Draw on process guides to frame the improvement. Process mapping, analysis and redesign
Collect mixed data (qualitative + operational) Interviews/observation (patients, caregivers, professionals), system data (times, referrals), complaints, and PREMs/PROMs (e.g., OECD PaRIS in PHC). Patient-Reported Indicator Surveys
Build the map(s)


Journey map (stages, emotions, barriers, capabilities).
Service blueprint (frontstage/backstage, actors, ICT, rules).
Process map (“as is”) with an expanded team (PHC, specialized care, regulation). Using Journey Mapping and Service Blueprinting to Design Digital Health Behavior Change Innovations: A Scoping Review


Equity and risk analysis Apply PROGRESS-Plus (residence, race/ethnicity, occupation, gender, education, income, social capital, disability, etc.) to see where the itinerary fails the most; identify safety risks at handoffs. Reporting and conducting patient journey mapping research in healthcare: A scoping review - PubMed
Co-create solutions and prioritize Use EBCD/workshops to generate and test countermeasures (pathway navigation; segmented checklists and messages; “one-stop” scheduling; active follow-up for no-shows; hybrid digital/in-person flows). Blueprints help estimate feasibility and dependencies. Experience-Based Co-Design of Health Care Services
Pilot, measure, and learn (LHS) Implement rapid tests (PDSA) and integrate journey data into a Learning Health System — cycles of collection → analysis → feedback → adjustment. Connect PREMs/PROMs (PaRIS) to flow metrics (lead time, successful handoffs) and outcomes. Exploring Patient Journey Mapping and the Learning Health System: Scoping Review
Scale and sustain Standards, kits, and EBCD and mapping toolkits support replication and training of clinical/management teams. Experience-based co-design toolkit

title: Therapeutic Itinerary
section: Common Pitfalls and How to Mitigate Them
text:
Common Pitfalls and How to Mitigate Them

Heterogeneous reporting/execution → adopt methodological checklists (objective, data, personas/journeys, validation, indicators). Reporting and conducting patient journey mapping research in healthcare: A scoping review - PubMed
Focus only on the “average” patient → include priority populations and structural barriers (transportation, income, connectivity), reflecting these in the map and solutions. Reporting and conducting patient journey mapping research in healthcare: A scoping review - PubMed
Map without change → connect PJM to improvement methods (Lean, PDSA), clinical governance, and implementation budgets. Conventional process mapping - aqua.nhs.uk
Non-actionable solutions → complement with blueprints and, when possible, process mining/simulation to test capacity, queues, and trade-offs before scaling. Using Journey Mapping and Service Blueprinting to Design Digital Health Behavior Change Innovations: A Scoping Review

title: Therapeutic Itinerary
text:
Essential References (Annotated Selection)

Bulto LN et al. Patient journey mapping — overview and six steps; foundation for structuring PJM projects. Eur J Cardiovasc Nurs. 2024. Patient journey mapping: emerging methods for understanding and improving patient experiences of health systems and services - PubMed
Davies EL et al. Scoping review on how to conduct and report PJM; shows acceleration in use and standardization gaps. J Adv Nurs. 2023. Reporting and conducting patient journey mapping research in healthcare: A scoping review - PubMed
Voorheis P et al. Scoping review on journey mapping + service blueprinting in digital behavior change interventions. 2025. Using Journey Mapping and Service Blueprinting to Design Digital Health Behavior Change Innovations: A Scoping Review
Philpot LM et al. Case of a patient-centered map (mixed methods) to focus experience improvements. 2019. Creation of a Patient-Centered Journey Map to Improve the Patient Experience: A Mixed Methods Approach
Duan Y et al. PJM applications in the breast cancer care pathway (synthesis of uses and lessons). BMJ Open. 2025. Application of patient journey mapping in patients with breast cancer: a scoping review
Holt B et al. Qualitative PJM methodology for viral hepatitis (Vietnam/Philippines) focused on co-design and context. 2025. Putting people at the center: methods for patient journey mapping of viral hepatitis services across two LMICs in the Asia Pacific
IHI / King’s Fund / Point of Care. EBCD guides (experience-based co-design) — step-by-step, cases, and tools. Experience-Based Co-Design of Health Care Services
NHS England / AQuA. Process mapping guides for mapping journeys/processes and initiating improvements safely. Process mapping, analysis and redesign
OECD PaRIS. Concept, analytical plan, and field results — PREMs/PROMs for monitoring experience and outcomes in PHC. Data analysis plan of the OECD PaRIS survey
Process mining / simulation. Analytical complements to enrich PJM and test scenarios. A Data-Driven Approach to Support the Understanding and Improvement of Patients’ Journeys: A Case Study Using Electronic Health Records of an Emergency Department

title: Therapeutic Itinerary
text:
In Summary (Practical Lessons)

Use PJM to align teams around itinerary goals (time to diagnosis; continuity; experience; equity).
Mix methods: journey + blueprint + process + data (PREMs/PROMs, EHR, times) + co-design.
Design for equity from the start (PROGRESS-Plus) and test capacity/flow before scaling.
Measure and learn: integrate PJM into a Learning Health System with PDSA cycles and actionable indicators. Exploring Patient Journey Mapping and the Learning Health System: Scoping Review

title: Nossas Personas
text:
Até o momento, definimos as seguintes Personas. Esta listagem foi criada no encontro de 22 de outubro de 2025. O objetivo destas personas é criar cenários diversos para podermos percorrer o itinerário de todos estes pacientes (personas) e identificar todas as barreiras, fragilidades e fortalezas já existentes aqui. Além disso, através delas poderemos criar em detalhes o novo modelo de cuidado.

Pedro, menino, terceiro filho, 10 meses de vida, baixo peso e baixa estatura. Já se senta, mas ainda não engatinha. Sua mãe está grávida novamente e não mama mais no peito. -> baixo peso, baixa estatura e atraso do desenvolvimento psicomotor.
Carlota, 38 anos de idade, 28 semanas de gestação, G3P2 com pressão arterial 140-90 mmHg, sem queixas. Medidas anteriores normais. Nenhuma outra morbidade. Casada com o pai dos dois primeiros filhos, que hoje têm 8 e 6 anos. Gestação com doença hipertensiva da gestação.
Antônio, 24 anos, casado, chega em consulta de triagem com tosse há mais de duas semanas, expectoração hemoptóica, febre, perda de peso, cansaço e muita sudorese noturna.
Marcela, 27 anos, queixa de corrimento vaginal há 1 mês e sangramento e dor durante as relações sexuais. Além disso, tem emagrecimento e inapetência há mais de um mês, desde que começou a ter relações sexuais com novo parceiro há 3 meses. Está com HIV mas ainda não sabe o diagnóstico. Além disso, está com doença inflamatória pélvica (DIP) – razão do corrimento e da dispareunia.
Miriam 16 anos, com amenorréia de há semanas, disúria e leucorreia e prurido. Teve duas ISTs já tratadas, com dois parceiros. Vive com os avós e é órfã de ambos os pais. Está grávida e com infecção urinária.
João, 72 anos, hipertenso usando hctz, nifedinina e lisinopril e diabético com metformina, na consulta atual veio com creatinina elevada com taxa de filtração glomerular de 40 mL-minuto-1.73M2.
Ana, 35 anos, professora, dor de garganta há 3 dias, febre 38ºC, odinofagia, sem tosse ou rinorreia, sem atb. Colega de trabalho com quadro semelhante. Hiperemia e exsudato purulento. Faringoamigdalite aguda.
Marta, 68 anos, mulher negra, hipertensa há 5 anos, tensão sempre acima de 180/110 mmHg, há um dia notou diminuição da força do hemicorpo esquerdo, desvio da comissura labial para a direita. Provável AVC ou AIT.
Paulo, 72 anos, viúvo, hipertenso com tensões em 130/80 mmHg, teve AVC há 6 meses. Agora com paresia à esquerda, marcha prejudicada. Vive com a irmã. Usa hctz 25 mg, nifedinipo 30 mg (1) e aspirina 100 mg (1) e sinvastatina 20 mg (1).
João, 6 anos, febre, dor articular, dor abdominal há 3 meses. Testam malária sempre com resultado negativo. Baço aumentado, dor à palpação abdominal, edema em mmii, inchaço dos dedos em mmss. descobriram que tinha anemia falciforme. Prescreveram hidroxiuréia e AINEs. Pela preocupação com possível sequestro esplênico, foi encaminhado à urgência para avaliação com o cirurgião.
Paulo 64 anos, viúvo, hipertenso há 20 anos e Diabético há 10 anos medicado com Lisinopril, Nifedipina e Hidroclorotiazida e Metformina. Na consulta actual com dor lombar e parestesias nos membros inferiores. Espondiloartrose anquilosante.
Angela 52 anos, desempregada, hipertenso há 13 anos e Diabética há 10 anos medicado com Lisinopril, Nifedipina e Hidroclorotiazida e Metformina e Glicazida. Foi mandada embora na AMODIA por falta de dinheiro das cotas mensais da associação. Decidiu fazer consultas no hospital geral da polana canico. Na consulta actual com parestesias nos membros inferiores. Ao exame físico com alteração da sensibilidade profunda e apresenta Ta:187/98 mmhg e Hemoglobina glicada de 13%.
